text: Hello and welcome to this episode of This is My Architecture. I'm Kapil and with me I have Budi
from Axileon. Budi, welcome to the show. Thank you for having me. Glad to have you here, Budi.
Can you tell us a little bit about Axileon? Axileon is an enterprise content product company. We
prevent data breaches and compliance pollution from third-party libraries. Organizations rely
on Axileon platform to complete visibility, security and control of their
communication of their sensitive data. Fantastic. And can you describe the CI, CD
platform that you run on your on-premise infrastructure today? Yeah, so this is
our developer. We have on-premise data center. We use GitLab and Jenkins and
server farm here. So our developer puts mid request into our GitLab and GitLab will run
parallel pipeline which will execute in our server farm here. This typically could run
up to like five minutes. Okay. And then Jenkins twice a day. It will pull the
repository from GitLab. It will do build and run full sanity tests and security scanning which could
take up to one hour. Okay. So after that's done Jenkins again will execute the job to run
regression and performance tests which could take up to seven hours. Okay. Okay. And what were the
challenges you were facing with this architecture? Yeah, as our company grow we have more
developer, we have more project. And what happened is we have more pipeline to run.
Whenever we don't have enough capacity in our server farm, right, this will get
queue. Right. And it's a big problem for developers, especially near like end of the
sprint because they have to wait. Yeah. So how did you solve these challenges? Were there any
architectural changes you had to make? Yeah, so we did the research and we found that
expanding to Amazon PPC is the best solution for us. Okay. Because
it can scale and also it's guaranteed the security by using side to side VPN. Okay. So
established a secure side to side VPN tunnel with AWS. Yes. Yeah. And we also isolate the
connection in and out from the PPC only coming from our infrastructure. And you use this
channel to make API calls to Amazon EC2 to launch instances, right? Yes. So yeah, we are using
plugin on our GitLab and Jenkins. Okay. And this will actually call the API here, which in turn,
it will launch EC2 to Spot instances as many as we need. Yeah. So speaking of Spot, can you tell us why did you choose Spot?
There are two reasons for this. One is the nature of our tests here doesn't require data retention. So we destroy after we do
tests. So just perfect for Spot instances. Okay. And second is cost. We can save up to 62% compared to if we build on-premise solution.
Yeah. That's awesome. So now you have a scalable and cost effective CI CD platform that pretty
much extends from your on-premise environment to the cloud in a transparent manner, right? That's correct.
